cells.tense: Something is arriving and you are deciding where to aim yourself at it.
cells.ask: Take one thing already arriving and make the small hard choice it needs this week — then let one steady person hold an edge of it with you.
cells.core:
You are pulled toward one direction over the others, and you are treating that pull as worth following. It did not come from a spreadsheet. It came as a draw toward a certain light, and you have been moving at it. What is arriving now does not need you to defend it. It needs you to say yes to it.

A hand on the heavy end is what steadies this. Holding what matters without forcing it is the practice — the direction stays yours, and the weight gets shared. Someone can hold an edge of this without taking the wheel. That is what keeps the aim clean and the arrival actually met. Let the help in before the load makes the call for you.
cells.sheetLine: You know where you're aiming. Let the weight be shared.
cells.verb: pointing yourself toward one light and holding there
cells.place: the threshold where something outside is coming in

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future that has not been written in yet.
cells.ask: Name one thing that is already arriving and meet it this week — before you have decided what it means.
cells.core:
You are living ahead of the present, checking what is about to arrive before it has landed. Every signal gets read for its consequences — who this makes you, what it forces, which future it closes off. The arrival is happening now; your attention is somewhere up the road doing risk assessment.

What settles this is plain knowing, not more prediction. Perceptions land on their own when you stop forcing them. Let one thing arrive without knowing yet what it is. Comfort with not-knowing is not a loss here; it is the exact stretch that lets the direction be chosen instead of guessed at. Hold the question open a day longer than feels safe.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Spend ten unforced minutes on one thing you have already grown — and stop there.
cells.core:
Something is arriving and you are not meeting it. You are facing the door you already came through — the last one, the hard one — and answering what is here now as if it were still that. The pull toward a new direction is real. You are just not at the open end of it.

The way back is not forcing yourself through the door again. It is showing up to the thing you have been tending, without forcing it, and noticing it already grew. Care that does not exhaust is the exact motion. Tend something small for ten minutes; let it be enough. Energy put there pulls the current back through the part of you that's been waiting, without pushing anything into it directly.
cells.sheetLine: You're facing the old door. Something here needs tending.

cells.tense: You are setting direction and calling it the weather, not the choosing.
cells.ask: Say out loud once that a direction you're already moving in is yours, then let one steady person help carry it.
cells.core:
You are already pointed — in what you say yes to, what you refuse, where your attention goes without being told. That is real aiming, and it is happening now. You describe it as if the pull came from outside, as if circumstances did the pointing and you just followed.

The simpler true thing is that you set this. Saying so out loud, once, is enough — not a declaration, just the plain fact to one person. Then let them hold some of the weight. Strength that contains rather than crushes is available from others. Take it. What you are already doing does not need defending. It needs to be called yours.
